column6: Dynamic-Memory Event-Triggered Fuzzy Adaptive Fault-Tolerant Control for Robotic Manipulators: A New Switching Mechanism
column13: Codificación ciega en sesión separada, asistida por IA generativa, sin acceso a la extracción ni a la clave; 2026-11-25. Editorial (IEEE TFUZZ 34(1) 2026, PDF). E4: Sec. V, 2-DOF arm with DC motors, QPIDe; faults injected by software. Model eq. (3)-(4): u=beta*Q*v+mu, beta in (0,1), bias mu; beta=0 total loss. Hardware scenario 1: u11=0 at 10 s (F5 of one of three channels), u21=0.8v21 (F1). Scenario 2 (Fig. 9, same platform): bias +0.2 (F2), u12=0.2 constant (stuck value, F4t), windows of 0.1-0.5 effectiveness and zero output (F6, F5). A3: switching among three modeled actuators per joint (Sec. III-C, Table I, Remark 2); trigger is a performance indicator on tracking error, no FDI (fault_information none). Doubt: the three actuators per joint are software channels on one motor; F4t could be read as F2/F6.

column6: Energy-Efficient and Fault-Tolerant Control of a Six-Axis Robot Based on AI Models
column13: Editorial (Energies 18(1):20, 2025, HTML MDPI). Fault = locked axis, angular position does not change (Sec. 2.7); 22 configurations: all axes, any one or two axes locked (Sec. 2.5). E_AMBIG: abstract says results verified on a real robot for 22 configurations, but Sec. 3 reports on the Mitsubishi RV-12SDL only nominal energy measurement; the damaged-j3 case is labeled simulation. Coded at the supported level E2 (MuJoCo torque model, Sec. 2.1-2.2); hw none. A3: step-wise replanning with the remaining axes; ANN1 (GA-trained) selects active axes, MLP predicts reward parameters (T-ML; A4 defensible). Per-axis real-vs-model position check detects and localizes the failed axis (Sec. 2.7) -> isolation.

column6: Adaptive PID actuator fault tolerant control of single-link flexible manipulator
column13: Editorial (Trans Inst Meas Control, OnlineFirst 2018, PDF). E1: MATLAB/Simulink simulation of a nominal model (Simulation results, Table 1 from Baroudi 2009). Fault eq. (9): x''=f+g*ha*u, 0<=ha<1 (F1). Table 2: Type A/B constant ha=0.3; Type C incipient ha varying with time (F6). A1: adaptive PID with Lyapunov adaptation, no fault information (abstract, eq. 10-28).

column6: Fault-tolerant analysis and control of SSRMS-type manipulators with single-joint failure
column13: Editorial (Acta Astronaut 2016, HTML via USACH proxy). Fault analysis of the 7-DOF SSRMS-type arm with a joint locked at arbitrary positions (Sec. 3, post-failure Jacobian); failed joint loses active control and swings with the coupling until locked (Sec. 4, three stages, Fig. 30) -> F4q and F5. Accommodation: self-motion adjustment of the failed joint into the safe region using underactuated dynamics, lock, then 6-DOF continuation; H-infinity controller for the underactuated stage (Sec. 4.1-4.2) -> A3 (redundancy: self-motion, fault-tolerant configuration). E1: numerical simulation of a simplified planar 3-DOF redundant arm, failure at t1 = 2 s (Sec. 5, Figs. 33-37). Failed joint given (known). Underactuation used transiently.

column6: A Simulative Study on Model-Based Emergency Strategies for Damage Prevention After Cable Breaks in Cable-Driven Parallel Robots
column13: Editorial (Robotics 15(9):180, 2026, HTML MDPI). Cable break of cable 4 simulated by setting its force to zero (Sec. 4). E2: MATLAB/Simulink multibody model with actuator dynamics, platform inertia and cable elasticity (Sec. 4); no hardware run with a break. Strategies (EMM NMPC, PFM, hybrid) recompute forces of the seven remaining cables (structure matrix without the broken cable) and drive the platform to a safe pose or halt; success = no crash within 2 s (Sec. 3, 4.1, 5) -> A3, task abandoned -> task relaxation (8 cables, 6 DOF: physical actuation redundancy also used). Break assumed known, no detection.

column6: Neural Dynamic Fault-Tolerant Scheme for Collaborative Motion Planning of Dual-Redundant Robot Manipulators
column13: Editorial (IEEE TNNLS 36(6), 2025, PDF read in the proxy viewer). Joint breakdown: velocities of faulty joints set to zero, A_L theta'_L = 0 (Sec. II-B, eq. 12), faulty joints assumed (q-th, p-th) -> known. A3: fault-tolerant QP with repetitive-motion criterion solved by VP-RNN, healthy joints compensate (Sec. II-III). 3-D simulation with dual Kinova Jaco and physical experiment on dual UFACTORY xArm 6 with joints locked in the same way (Sec. IV-C, Figs. 16-17, faulty joint marked) -> E4, hw F4q.

column6: Adaptive fuzzy terminal sliding mode control for the free-floating space manipulator with free-swinging joint failure
column13: Editorial (Chin J Aeronaut 34(9), 2021, PDF). F5: free-swinging joints, underactuated space manipulator (abstract, Sec. 2). E1: numerical simulation of SSRMS-type 7-DOF model (Sec. 5), no physics engine. Controller TSMC/AFTSMC designed on the post-fault underactuated model with the passive joints given (known); adaptive fuzzy estimates uncertainty, not the fault. A2 chosen as post-fault reconfiguration with known fault; A1 defensible (fixed robust adaptive law, no FDI).

column6: A Fault-Tolerant Method for Motion Planning of Industrial Redundant Manipulator
column13: Editorial (IEEE TII 16(12), 2020, PDF). Joint failure as theta_i'=0 for t>tf (Sec. II-B). A3: fault-tolerant redundancy resolution QP with primal-dual NN (Sec. III-A). Observer estimates failure state matrix and localizes faulty joints (Sec. III-C, Alg. 1) -> isolation. Experiment on Kuka LBR iiwa with joints 3, 6, 7 failed during circle drawing (Sec. V, Figs. 5-7) -> E4, hw F4q.

column6: Intelligent Fault Diagnosis and Fault-Tolerant Control of Robotic Manipulators Based on Deep Neural Networks
column13: Editorial (MRAI 2026 proceedings, PDF in proxy viewer). Six fault categories diagnosed by CNN-LSTM: joint wear, reducer fault, encoder drift, controller failure, collision, overload (Sec. II-A). Accommodation: MPC compensation selected by the diagnosed fault type (feedforward gain for wear, sensor-fusion position reconstruction for encoder drift, safe degradation for severe faults) (Sec. II-C) -> A2, isolation (fault classification). Platform KUKA KR10 R1100 with encoders, torque sensors (Sec. III-A, Table II); Table V reports tracking under joint wear, encoder drift and reducer fault -> E4, hw F7 (wear, reducer) and F8. E_AMBIG: how faults were produced on the robot is not described. F0 for controller failure/overload named without a model.

column6: Fault-Tolerant, Rigidity-Preserving Control of Inflatable Truss Robots
column13: arXiv 2605.20561 v1, carries RA-L acceptance metadata and DOI (accepted version). Failed roller motor enforced as d_i'=0 (Sec. IV-C), A_broken x'=0 in the QP (Sec. IV-E) -> locked joint F4q. Hardware: 2D isoperimetric truss testbed, six active rollers, Vive tracking (Sec. IV-G); runs with roller 1 broken, rollers 1&4 broken, and roller 6 at 66% speed (Table I, Sec. V-D) -> E4, hw F4q and F1 (partial speed loss, not modeled by the controller). A3: redistribution among remaining rollers with DTCBF rigidity constraint. Failures injected with ground-truth knowledge (Sec. IV-C) -> known. Reserve: six rollers for a 2-DOF vertex task (doubt: physical actuation redundancy).

column6: A sensorless approach for cable failure detection and identification in cable-driven parallel robots
column13: Editorial (Robot Auton Syst 183, 2025, PDF). Cable failure of a 3-DOF suspended CDPR with four cables (Sec. 4, Fig. 9); failure produced by an electromagnet releasing cable 4 (Sec. 4, 5) -> E4, hw F7 (F7c). Sensorless FDI with digital twin identifies the broken cable (Sec. 3.1, isolation). Accommodation: end-effector recovery strategy, replanning toward a safe pose inside the residual SEW with tension-space planning (Sec. 3.2, 5.3) -> A3 (motion replanning), task abandoned -> task relaxation. Doubt: A2 defensible (detection paper; recovery from previous work).

column6: Cable failure tolerant control and planning in a planar reconfigurable cable driven parallel robot
column13: Editorial (Front Robot AI 10:1070627, 2023, HTML). Cable failure as linear drop of cable stiffness to zero (Sec. 3.2), one or two cables (Sec. 4.1). E2: MATLAB plant with slider second-order dynamics and velocity/position limits, winch first-order lag, elastic cables, process and measurement noise (Sec. 3, 6.1); simulation only (Sec. 2). IMM estimator identifies the failed cable from end-effector pose (Sec. 5, 6.2) -> isolation. Accommodation: reconfiguration of anchor points on linear sliders, bank of feedforward controllers mixed by IMM weights, LQR, replanning back to the break point; task continued (Sec. 5.1-5.5) -> A3 (reconfigurable actuation); A2 defensible.

column6: Fault-tolerant path planning for cable-driven manipulators based on a diffusion strategy
column13: Editorial (Mech Syst Signal Process, 15 Jan 2026, HTML via USACH proxy). Cable wear or damage in a hyper-redundant cable-driven manipulator (abstract, Sec. 1) -> F7 (F7c). Accommodation: physics-informed tension network plus tension-guided denoising diffusion that generates joint-space trajectories reducing the load on damaged cables (Sec. 3) -> A4 (the fault-tolerant path is generated by the learned diffusion model; A3 defensible, it exploits hyper-redundancy). Self-developed five-joint cable-driven platform with tension sensors (Sec. 4, Fig. 6, Table 1); Sec. 5.2: cable 11 designated damaged, ROS simulation and real-world validation of the planned path (Fig. 10) -> E4, hw F7 (doubt: damage is designated in planning, not physically produced). Damaged cables given (known).

column6: Robust Adaptive Fuzzy Fault Tolerant Control of Robot Manipulators With Unknown Parameters
column13: Editorial (IEEE TFUZZ 31(9), 2023, PDF in proxy viewer). Actuator fault u_i = xi_i u_ci + delta_i(t), xi in (0,1], bias (Sec. II-B, eq. 6-7), plus incipient process fault gamma(t-T)phi (eq. 1-4, not an actuator class). E1: simulation of a three-link planar manipulator (Sec. IV). Simulation 1: xi = 1 before 15 s and time-varying (about 0.6 sin t) after, delta = 0.3 after 15 s (eq. 72) -> F1, F2, F6. A1: robust adaptive fuzzy FTC with constraint mechanism, no fault information (abstract, Sec. III).

column6: Sliding Mode Control for Robot Manipulators with Actuator Faults
column13: Editorial (CCC 2021 proceedings, PDF in proxy viewer). Fault u = F(t) tau, 0 < f_i <= 1 (Sec. 2, eq. 5), lumped into a disturbance. E1: MATLAB simulation of a two-link manipulator (Sec. 5). Case 1: f = 0.2 after 10 s; case 2: f = 0.4 + 0.2 sin(2 pi t) after 10 s (eq. 36-37) -> F1, F6. A1: nonsingular terminal SMC with dynamic gain, no fault information (Sec. 3).

column6: Active robust fault-tolerant control strategy of redundantly actuated distributed parallel manipulators for large-scale component assembly
column13: Editorial (Nonlinear Dyn 114:1086, 2026, PDF). Fault eq. (11): u=chi*uc+u_delta (F1, F2). Experiment Sec. 6.1: self-built 4-PPPS RADPM, artificial time-varying faults on six joints of L1 and L3 after 5 s: chi=rand[0.55,0.75]+0.03 sin(5t), bias rand+0.02 sin(3t) (F1, F2, F6 on hardware). A2: nonlinear observer detection (Theorem 1) + adaptive LOE estimator (Sec. 3.2) activating NFTSM with NN compensation (Fig. 2). Reserve: the platform is redundantly actuated but the scheme compensates each faulty actuator by increased input, no reallocation -> full actuation (doubt: physical actuation redundancy).

column6: A new hybrid neurodynamics-based model-less solution for redundant robot fault-tolerant motion planning and control
column13: Editorial (ISA Trans 166, 2025, PDF). Joint failure as zero joint velocity Mq'=0 (eq. 12-14). Simulation Kinova Jaco Gen2 (Sec. 4.1); experiment on 7-DOF Kinova Jaco Gen3 with q3 and q3+q5 failed (Sec. 4.2, Figs. 7-8) -> E4, hw F4q. A3: QP redundancy resolution solved by ZND; Jacobian estimated by GND (data-driven, T-ML) but accommodation is redundancy resolution. Fault state matrix M predefined (known).

column6: Failure treatment strategy and fault-tolerant path planning of a space manipulator with free-swinging joint failure
column13: Editorial open access (Chin J Aeronaut 31(12), 2018, HTML via USACH proxy). Free-swinging joint failure (abstract, Sec. 1-2). Treatment: optimal locked angle from degraded manipulability and workspace (Sec. 2.2), underactuated adjustment of the passive joint by dynamics-model reconfiguration and PD with coupling (Sec. 3), lock, then fault-tolerant A* path planning in the degraded workspace (DWWIKP, Sec. 4) -> A3 (fault-tolerant configuration and replanning). E1: numerical simulation of the 7-DOF SSRMS-type arm, J2 failed (Sec. 5, Tables 2-3, Figs. 3-6). Fault joint confirmed as input (Sec. 4 Step 1) -> known. Locking is part of the accommodation, so F4q not coded.

column6: Adaptive Compensation for Infinite Number of Actuator Faults and Time-Varying Delay of a Flexible Manipulator System
column13: Editorial (IEEE TIE 69(12), 2022, PDF in proxy viewer). Infinite number of time-varying actuator faults u = rho_k(t) u_c + u_f,k(t) on [t_k, t_k+1) (Sec. II, eq. 6). Simulation cases 1-2: switching effectiveness 0.5/0.3/0.1 plus decaying bias 0.1 e^-2t, periodic (eq. 36-37) -> F1, F2, F6. Experiment on Quanser rotary flexible link with the same fault cases (Sec. V, Fig. 6, Table III) -> E4 (doubt E3: single-link apparatus). A1: adaptive compensation with projection and RBFNN, no FDI (Sec. III; doubt A2, adaptive parameter covers fault bounds).

column6: Fault-Tolerant Control for Redundant Manipulators via Feasible Space Expansion Strategy: A Dynamic Desensitization Approach
column13: Accepted version (IEEE TII early access 2026, PDF). Joint lockup as Aq'=0 (Sec. II-B, eq. 9c). Kinova Jaco2 runs are path-indexed simulation curves (Sec. V-A); physical run on xArm6 in joint-velocity mode with J2 locked at tau=30 (Sec. V-D6, Fig. 9) -> E4, hw F4q. A3: redundancy resolution TVQP plus execution-rate scaling v (task relaxation is the added element; reserve coded as kinematic redundancy, task relaxation secondary). Locked joints given in A (known).
